newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH FOREST CHIEF SAYS MARKKA TOO FIRM FOR ERM.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH FOREST CHIEF SAYS MARKKA TOO FIRM FOR ERM.

text.p: The Finnish markka is currently too strong to enter Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM), Juha Niemela, chief executive of UPM-Kymmene Oy , Europe's biggest forest industry group, said on Wednesday.
"At the moment, I would say (the markka) is too strong. If linked to ERM at this level it might face downward pressure," Niemela told Reuters. He declined to say what would be an appropriate level.
"A strong markka is bad for the forest industry," Niemela said. The markka closed at 3.027 against the German mark and at 4.559 against the U.S. dollar.
The Finnish government has said a decision whether to link the markka to ERM will be made this autumn.
The highly cyclical forest industry is among the country's most important foreign currency earners accounting for about one third of annual export revenues.
In Europe, Finland's biggest forest industry competitor is Sweden, which is undecided on whether to join Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
